question: What happens to the glomerular filtration rate during a normal pregnancy?
explanation: Pregnancy causes the kidneys to work harder, increasing the glomerular filtration rate so that waste products are cleared much faster from the blood. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why might a normal non-pregnant serum creatinine level be a warning sign during pregnancy?

options.A: Normal pregnancy lowers creatinine levels, so a standard value actually reflects reduced kidney function
options.B: Pregnancy causes the liver to produce excess creatinine which masks kidney disease
options.C: Creatinine is never measured in pregnant women because it is completely unreliable
options.D: Standard values are too low to detect normal fetal kidney waste elimination

explanation: Because healthy pregnant kidneys filter blood much faster, normal serum creatinine drops. A value in the upper normal non-pregnant range actually points to sluggish kidney function. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h1)

question: What defines asymptomatic bacteriuria in an expectant mother?

options.A: Presence of bacteria in the urine without clinical symptoms of infection
options.B: Inability to pass urine despite a full bladder
options.C: Frequent painful urination accompanied by high fever
options.D: Severe lower abdominal pain with blood in the urine

explanation: Asymptomatic bacteriuria means bacteria are multiplying in the urine, but the woman feels completely fine and has no typical urinary symptoms. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h2)

question: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks has bacteria in her urine lab test but feels completely well. What is the appropriate midwifery action?

options.A: Wait until the third trimester before giving any medication
options.B: Commence appropriate antibiotic treatment to prevent pyelonephritis
options.C: Ignore the result since she has no symptoms to treat
options.D: Advise her to drink palm wine exclusively to flush the kidneys

explanation: Even without symptoms, treating bacteriuria in pregnancy is crucial because it frequently escalates into dangerous kidney infections if left alone. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h2)

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of acute pyelonephritis during pregnancy?

options.A: Painless bright red bleeding from the vagina
options.B: Costovertebral angle tenderness with high fever
options.C: Severe itching all over the abdomen
options.D: Painless swelling of both lower limbs

explanation: Pyelonephritis is a kidney infection, making the area over the kidneys in the back very tender, alongside systemic signs like high fever. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h3)

question: Why is acute pyelonephritis considered an emergency requiring hospital admission?

options.A: It makes the baby stop moving permanently
options.B: It always causes permanent kidney failure within twenty-four hours
options.C: It can rapidly cause maternal sepsis and trigger preterm labour
options.D: Oral medications are strictly forbidden for pregnant women

explanation: The systemic inflammation and high fevers of pyelonephritis pose severe threats to both mother and baby, requiring close inpatient monitoring and intravenous drugs. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h3)

question: Which complication is most commonly superimposed on chronic kidney disease during pregnancy?
explanation: Damaged blood vessels and altered renal dynamics make women with chronic kidney disease highly vulnerable to developing pre-eclampsia. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h4)

question: Why are ACE inhibitors avoided for managing high blood pressure in pregnant women with kidney disease?

options.A: They cause the mother's blood pressure to drop to zero instantly
options.B: They have no effect on blood pressure during pregnancy
options.C: They turn the amniotic fluid dark green and toxic
options.D: They cause severe birth defects affecting the baby's kidneys

explanation: ACE inhibitors interfere with fetal kidney development and are well known to cause severe fetal injury and low amniotic fluid levels. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h4)

question: What is a primary obstetric cause of acute kidney injury in low-resource settings?
explanation: Uncontrolled bleeding leads to profound hypovolaemic shock, starving the kidneys of blood flow and causing acute tubular injury. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h5)

question: A woman after delivery passes very little urine over a 4-hour period despite drinking well. What is the immediate midwifery priority?

options.A: Discharge her home with instructions to drink plenty of water
options.B: Reassure the relatives that the kidneys are resting after the hard work of labour
options.C: Assess vital signs, review fluid balance, and report the low urine output urgently
options.D: Wait for another six hours to see if her bladder fills up naturally

explanation: Low urine output is a cardinal sign of acute kidney injury requiring rapid clinical evaluation to prevent permanent renal damage. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T10#BMP221_U4_T10_h5)
